zh: 一个格子的状态只会被两类事件改变：它自己被杀（变死），以及它的某个严格祖先被杀（让它复活）。K 是排列，这些事件的时刻互不相同，最终状态由其中最晚发生的那一个决定。
只要知道每个格子所有严格祖先里最大的 K：若它大于格子自身的 K，最后一次影响来自祖先，格子存活；否则格子最后一次被自己杀死，状态为死。严格祖先的集合正好是三个合法父格各自“自身加全部祖先”集合的并，所以可以逐行递推最大值，不必逐个事件模拟。

自上而下逐行扫描，保留上一行数组 previous，previous[c] 表示上一行第 c 格及其全部祖先的最大 K，越界位置当作 0。当前格的祖先最大值取 previous[c−1]、previous[c]、previous[c+1] 三者最大；若它大于自身 K 输出 1，否则输出 0；再把该最大值与自身 K 取大存入当前行数组，供下一行使用。每组测试开始时把 previous 清零，总时间 O(Σnm)。
en: A cell's state is changed by only two kinds of events: the cell itself being killed (it becomes dead) and one of its strict ancestors being killed (which revives it). Since K is a permutation, these events all happen at distinct times, and the final state is decided by whichever of them happens last.

All you need for each cell is the maximum K among its strict ancestors: if it is larger than the cell's own K, the last event comes from an ancestor and the cell is alive; otherwise the cell was last killed by itself and is dead. The set of strict ancestors is exactly the union of the "self plus all ancestors" sets of its three valid parents, so the maximum can be carried row by row without simulating events one at a time.

Scan the rows from top to bottom while keeping an array previous for the row above, where previous[c] is the maximum K over cell c of that row and all of its ancestors, with out-of-range positions treated as 0. For the current cell, the ancestor maximum is the largest of previous[c-1], previous[c] and previous[c+1]; print 1 if it exceeds the cell's own K, otherwise print 0; then store the larger of that maximum and the cell's own K in the current row's array for the next row. Reset previous at the start of every test case; the total time is O(sum of nm).

explanationEn:
## Source recovery and rules

The fixed raw source keeps the full constraints: 1≤T≤1000, 1≤n,m≤1000, Σ(nm)≤10^6 over all test cases, and in each test case K is a permutation of 1 to nm. Initially every cell is alive; cells are killed in increasing order of K, and after each kill all strict descendants of that cell become alive. The children are the valid cells directly below-left, below and below-right in the next row, and the recursive propagation does not stop just because some intermediate cell was already alive. The killed cell itself is not revived, and overlapping reachable paths only affect the state of the same cell; they do not create multiple entities.

The raw source writes the bottom-right corner as (n,m), while the example calls the second cell of the first row (1,2); these are typos in the coordinate text. This site uses 0-based coordinates 0≤r<n, 0≤c<m throughout and keeps the original K matrices and outputs unchanged. Simulating the original sample event by event gives 000/000/101, which agrees with the recursive strict-descendant rule. The second and third examples on this site separately distinguish propagation from distant ancestors and the reset of state between test cases.

## Algorithm

For each cell we only need the largest K among all of its strict ancestors. The cell is killed at the time of its own K, and the kill of every strict ancestor revives it. Therefore the cell ends up alive if and only if the maximum K over its strict ancestors is greater than its own K.

Scan from top to bottom, with previous[c] holding the maximum K over cell c of the previous row and all of its ancestors. The maximum over the strict ancestors of the current cell is just the maximum of previous[c−1], previous[c] and previous[c+1], with out-of-range positions taken as 0. After computing the state, current[c] takes the maximum of that value and the cell's own K, for use by the next row. Reset the previous-row array for every test case. No sorting or event-by-event simulation is needed.

## Proof of correctness

A cell's state is affected by only two kinds of events: its own event sets it to 0, and the event of a strict ancestor sets it to 1; no other event affects it. Because K is a permutation, the times of these events are all distinct, so the final state is uniquely determined by the one that happens last: it is 1 when the maximum K over the strict ancestors is greater than its own K, and 0 otherwise.

The first row has no ancestors, so the boundary maximum of 0 is correct. Suppose each cached value of the previous row contains the maximum K over that cell and all of its ancestors. Any ancestor path reaching the current cell must pass last through one of its three valid parents; conversely, every parent and each of its ancestors can reach the current cell. So merging the three cached values yields exactly the maximum K over all strict ancestors, and overlap between these sets does not affect the max. Taking the max with the cell's own K then gives the correct cached value for the current cell and its ancestors. By induction over the rows, all states are correct, and resetting independently keeps test cases from affecting each other.

## Complexity and boundary verification

Total time is O(Σnm), and the recurrence uses O(m) extra space; this Python implementation additionally uses O(Σnm) for input tokenization and the output buffer. It fully supports 1000×1000 grids as well as T=1000 with a million cells in total. Event times are at most 10^6, so there is no large-integer counting.

An independent oracle performs the actual kills in time order and walks along child edges to revive every strict descendant one by one, without using the ancestor-maximum recurrence. The structured expected outputs at maximum scale are constructed independently: when K increases by row, every ancestor is killed earlier, so everything ends up dead; when K decreases by row, the next row always has a later parent event, so only the first row is dead; when the top-left corner is killed last and the rest increase by row, only its strict descendant cone r>0 and c≤r is alive; with a thousand reversed single-column test cases, only the first cell of each test case is dead.
